subject: Food Science
title: Enzymes in Food
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Enzymes in Food.

hook.text: Cut an apple and it turns brown in minutes. An enzyme called polyphenol oxidase is the culprit.

buildup.text: Enzymes are protein catalysts that speed up chemical reactions. Food is full of them—even after harvest.

discovery.text: Papain from papaya breaks down tough meat fibers. That's why papaya juice is used as a meat tenderizer.

twist.text: Heat kills enzymes. Blanching vegetables before freezing stops enzyme activity that would ruin texture and color.

climax.text: Cheese-making depends on rennet—an enzyme that curdles milk by clotting the casein protein.

punchline.text: Enzymes build food, break food, and make food. Tiny proteins, huge impact.

quiz.question: Why do we blanch vegetables before freezing?
options: To kill enzymes that would ruin texture and color
